summary:
Paraná is a state of Brazil and stands under the national framework carried by the parent record; the findings below are those specific to the state and its municipalities.

Access to sex-separated facilities has been contested in Paraná's own legislature and municipal councils. In 2021 state representative Mara Lima introduced a bill prohibiting unisex bathrooms statewide and requiring separate male and female facilities. On 16 November 2021 the Curitiba City Council approved a municipal bill of the same kind introduced by councilman Ezequias Barros. Both measures target unisex provision and would require sex-separated bathrooms, which bears directly on how trans people use facilities.

On 4 October 2023 the Curitiba City Council approved a symbolic protest motion against Resolution 2/2023 of the Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship, which recommended that educational institutions guarantee use of bathrooms, changing rooms and other gender-segregated spaces according to each student's gender identity and expression, with additional individual-use bathrooms recommended in public spaces. The ministry stated the resolution has no binding effect and that no school is obliged to adopt it. The Curitiba motion was to be converted into an official letter to the federal government.

The Court of Justice of the State of Paraná has moved in both directions on gender markers. In 2023 it published a provision guaranteeing inclusion of 'non-binary' in the civil registry gender marker, then revoked it in November 2023, limiting administrative replacement of first name and sex to 'male' and 'female' only. In 2025 the same court authorised a third gender option on documents.

On 26 April 2024 Londrina enacted a municipal law barring transgender people from competing in sports according to gender identity, with a fine of R$10,000 for non-compliance. In March 2026 LGBTQ rights organisations challenged the law at the Supreme Federal Court, and on 7 August 2026 rapporteur Justice Cristiano Zanin voted to strike it down.

On 26 February 2026 the Londrina City Council approved a motion to bar transgender athlete Tiffanny Abreu from the Brazilian Women's Volleyball Cup. The Brazilian Volleyball Confederation filed suit at the Supreme Federal Court, and Justice Cármen Lúcia issued a preliminary injunction the same day allowing her to compete.

Marriage and stable-union recognition in Paraná follow the ordinary procedures. On 26 March 2013 the General Inspector of Justice of Paraná ruled that same-sex marriage and the conversion of stable unions into marriage must use the normal marriage procedure and documentation in all registry offices statewide, without judicial authorisation. The first recognition of a same-sex union in Brazil was granted in Curitiba in 2004, when an English-Brazilian couple cohabiting for fourteen years was given common-law marriage status previously limited to opposite-sex couples.
tangentialFactors:
Paraná's courts were early movers on relationship recognition. The 2004 Curitiba decision granting common-law marriage status to a couple of the same sex preceded nationwide marriage equality by nine years, and the 2013 ruling by the state's General Inspector of Justice opened marriage procedures in every registry office. Municipal councils have moved in the opposite direction more recently, approving measures against unisex facilities and against transgender athletes.

Litigation over Paraná's municipal measures has concentrated at the Supreme Federal Court, which suspended the Londrina sports ban by injunction and heard argument on its constitutionality. The Curitiba protest motion against the national school-facilities resolution was addressed to the federal government rather than to any Paraná institution.
localsOnly: Adoption by same-sex couples in Paraná was established through a series of first-instance decisions. On 14 May 2009 the 2nd Court of Childhood, Youth and Adoption granted the state's first adoption by a gay couple, to a couple in Curitiba, finding a stable and affectionate union able to raise a child in a healthy environment. On 27 October 2010 a Cascavel court authorised the irreversible adoption of an eight-year-old child with cerebral palsy by a gay couple together twelve years, granted by Judge Sergio Luiz Kreuz under Superior Court of Justice precedent. On 16 September 2011 a Maringá court authorised the adoption of two children by a lesbian couple.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 2021 state bill and the Curitiba municipal bill on unisex bathrooms were enacted, and their current status, is not sourced.

The scope and current force of the Court of Justice of the State of Paraná's 2025 authorisation of a third gender option on documents is not sourced.

Justice Cristiano Zanin's 7 August 2026 vote to strike down the Londrina sports ban is a rapporteur's vote; the final ruling of the Supreme Federal Court is not sourced.

Whether the Curitiba City Council's 4 October 2023 protest motion was converted into an official letter to the federal government, and any response to it, is not sourced.
